raw_response:
I farm on a small 3.5 mu wheat-maize rotation with well irrigation, so I would keep my plan simple, stable, and yield-focused. I have enough farming experience that I would not take risks with seed or input cuts at the start of the season. For wheat, I would use improved seed, give enough nitrogen for strong tillering and grain filling, add phosphorus for roots, keep potassium moderate, irrigate at the key stages, and use rotary tillage because it fits a small farm and saves labor. After wheat harvest, I would plant hybrid maize on the same land because hybrid maize gives me more reliable yield on limited area. I would put most fertilizer into maize nitrogen, keep irrigation to the main water-sensitive stages, and control weeds and insects with a limited number of pesticide sprays. Since some family members work off-farm, I would avoid overly labor-intensive management and choose a practical plan that protects output and fits my household labor.
